# Azure Functions

**Parity grade: B** · SDK `azure-sdk-for-go/sdk/resourcemanager/appservice/armappservice/v6@v6.0.0` · last audited 2026-11-05 (`959104c86`)

### Known gaps

- Background triggers are verified against a real node host (timer, queue, blob, Service Bus, Event Hubs; triggers_docker_test.go, opt-in GOPHERSTACK_AZFN_DOCKER_TEST=1), but the host starts at deploy only when a function.json declares a non-HTTP trigger; a code-first (v4 programming model) app with timer or queue triggers starts on its first request. Cosmos DB, Event Grid and other bundle extensions were not exercised.
- Remote build is not implemented: Python and Node dependencies must be packed into the zip (SCM_DO_BUILD_DURING_DEPLOYMENT is ignored; RemoteBuild=true on publish is 400).
- WEBSITE_RUN_FROM_PACKAGE=<URL> is fetched at host start with the emulator's own HTTP client (any http(s) URL, size capped, the URL kept out of errors); the package is not re-fetched until the host restarts. Flex apps should not set it (Learn: deprecated for Flex) but this is not enforced.
- The listener is plain HTTP; Kudu supports zipdeploy, publish?type=zip, deployments, the site zip download and vfs below site/wwwroot (no command, logstream, webjobs or vfs outside wwwroot).
- Windows function apps and Functions runtime versions other than ~4 run in the same Linux v4 images.
- Not implemented: app-level managed identity, VNet integration, custom domains and certificates, easy auth (authsettings are stored only); Flex Consumption deployment.storage is validated but not used as the package store, and alwaysReady, maximumInstanceCount and perInstanceConcurrency have no runtime effect.
- Container-reachable address: loopback hosts in app settings are rewritten to AZURE_FUNCTIONS_CONTAINER_HOST (default LAMBDA_DOCKER_HOST or 172.17.0.1, host.docker.internal on macOS and Windows); other runtimes (Kubernetes pods) are not verified, and Service Bus and Event Hubs connection strings need an explicit port (UseDevelopmentEmulator=true) because the emulator's AMQP ports are not the SDK defaults.
- Deployment slots: no auto swap, no testing-in-production traffic routing (x-ms-routing-name), no slot-level custom domains; slotsdiffs lists only the swapped settings that differ (diffRule and description strings are not verified against Azure) and not the sticky-setting changes of the preview phases; function and host keys, Kudu deployment history and the publishing password stay with their slot on a swap (unverified against Azure); connection strings are stored and swapped but are not injected into the container environment (no SQLCONNSTR_ style variables); the slot-limit and swap-conflict error codes (409 Conflict) are not verified against Azure; a swap holds the Microsoft.Web provider lock while it warms the source slot.
- Web apps: private registries (DOCKER_REGISTRY_SERVER_* credentials, ACR managed identity) are not supported, so only images the local runtime can pull anonymously start; EXPOSE auto-detection is not done (DOCKER apps use WEBSITES_PORT, PORT or 80).
- Web apps: no remote build (Oryx), so Node and Python dependencies must be inside the zip; Python apps need appCommandLine or an app.py/main.py entry (no gunicorn auto-detection); Tomcat, JBoss, Ruby and Go stacks, Windows web apps, multi-container (sitecontainers) and docker-compose apps are rejected with 400.
- Web apps: alwaysOn does not keep a container warm (hosts are never reaped anyway) and is not validated against the plan tier; an unhealthy running instance is not evicted or restarted after startup.
- Hosts are never reaped while idle; a stopped, redeployed or deleted app, or an emulator shutdown, removes them.
- No dashboard page.
